source.text: Καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ἐκεῖθεν, καὶ ἔρχεται εἰς τὴν πατρίδα αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἀκολουθοῦσιν αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And he went out from there, and comes into the hometown of him, and follow him the disciples of him.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went out from there and comes into {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hometown, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples follow {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Jesus left that place and went to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hometown, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples went with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Jesus left there and went back to Nazareth, the town where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} grew up. His followers went with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: hometown: Nazareth, where Jesus grew up
decisions.reason: The word means one's native place. Mark has named Nazareth as Jesus' home town (1:9, 1:24), and the synagogue scene that follows fits a small town.

decisions.choice: comes, follow: present tense in a story about the past
decisions.reason: Mark often tells past events in the present tense to make them vivid. The sense is past: he came, and they followed.

decisions.choice: from there: from the house of Jairus by the lake (5:21-43)
decisions.reason: The last place named is the lakeshore town where Jairus' daughter was raised.

decisions.choice: Nazareth, the town where he grew up
decisions.reason: Readable names the town so that new readers know where Jesus went.

source.text: καὶ γενομένου σαββάτου ἤρξατο διδάσκειν ἐν τῇ συναγωγῇ· καὶ οἱ πολλοὶ ἀκούοντες ἐξεπλήσσοντο λέγοντες· Πόθεν τούτῳ ταῦτα, καὶ τίς ἡ σοφία ἡ δοθεῖσα τούτῳ, καὶ αἱ δυνάμεις τοιαῦται διὰ τῶν χειρῶν αὐτοῦ γινόμεναι;

records.literal_gloss: And having come [the] Sabbath he began to teach in the synagogue; and the many hearing were astonished, saying, From where to this [man] these things, and what the wisdom the [one] having been given to this [man], and the miracles such through the hands of him coming about?

en.L: And when the Sabbath came, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} began to teach in the synagogue; and the many who heard were astonished, saying, "Where [did] this [man get] these things, and what [is] the wisdom given to this [man], and such works of power coming about through {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hands?"
en.B: When the Sabbath came, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} began teaching in the synagogue, and most of those who heard {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} were struck with amazement. "Where did this man get all this?" they said. "What is this wisdom that has been given to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}? And what are these mighty works that {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hands are doing?"
en.R: On the Sabbath day Jesus began to teach in the synagogue. Many people heard {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and they were amazed. They said, "Where did {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} learn all this? Who gave {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} such wisdom? How can {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} do these powerful miracles with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hands?"

decisions.choice: astonished: struck with amazement, not yet trust
decisions.reason: The same word as at 1:22. Here amazement turns into offense (6:3).

decisions.choice: the many: most of those present
decisions.reason: With the article the phrase means the majority of the hearers.

decisions.choice: works of power: miracles that show God's power
decisions.reason: The word means powers or mighty deeds. Mark uses it for Jesus' miracles (6:5, 6:14).

decisions.choice: given to this man: the people half admit that his wisdom is a gift from outside himself
decisions.reason: The passive leaves the giver unnamed. The townspeople ask where it came from because they know his family (6:3).

decisions.choice: mighty works (B); powerful miracles (R)
decisions.reason: The word joins the idea of power with the deeds it produces.

source.text: οὐχ οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ τέκτων, ὁ υἱὸς τῆς Μαρίας καὶ ἀδελφὸς Ἰακώβου καὶ Ἰωσῆτος καὶ Ἰούδα καὶ Σίμωνος;

records.literal_gloss: Not this is the carpenter, the son of Mary and brother of James and Joses and Judas and Simon?

en.L: Is this not the carpenter, the son of Mary and brother of James and Joses and Judas and Simon?
en.B: Is {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} not the carpenter, the son of Mary, and a brother of James, Joses, Judas and Simon?
en.R: He is just the carpenter, is {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} not? He is Mary's son. His brothers are James, Joses, Judas and Simon.

decisions.choice: the carpenter, the son of Mary: the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: the son of the carpenter and of Mary
decisions.reason: A few manuscripts read "the son of the carpenter", which matches Matthew 13:55. Scribes may have changed it so that Jesus himself was not called a craftsman. The SBLGNT follows the great majority of manuscripts. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: Joses, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts read Joseph, as in Matthew 13:55. Joses is a short form of the same name. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: carpenter: a builder or craftsman in wood or stone
decisions.reason: The word covers anyone who builds, in wood most often but also in stone. The point is that he is a working man they know.

decisions.choice: son of Mary: unusual, since a man was normally named by his father
alternatives: the ordinary way to name him
decisions.reason: Joseph is not mentioned. He may have died by this time, or the words may carry a slight on Jesus' birth. Mark does not say.

decisions.choice: brother: the ordinary word for a brother in the same family
alternatives: a son of Joseph by an earlier marriage
decisions.reason: The word normally means a brother. Some Christian traditions understand these men as cousins or as Joseph's sons by an earlier marriage. The text names them brothers and does not settle the question.

decisions.choice: just the carpenter, is he not?
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer yes and is meant to belittle. Readable makes the tone plain with "just".

source.text: καὶ οὐκ εἰσὶν αἱ ἀδελφαὶ αὐτοῦ ὧδε πρὸς ἡμᾶς;

records.literal_gloss: And not are the sisters of him here with us?

en.L: And are {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} sisters not here with us?
en.B: And are {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} sisters not here among us?
en.R: And {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} sisters live here in our town, do they not?

decisions.choice: his sisters: unnamed, but living in the town
decisions.reason: Mark names the brothers but not the sisters. They still live in Nazareth, among the people speaking.

decisions.choice: here with us: living among us
decisions.reason: The point is that the family is ordinary and well known in the town.

decisions.choice: live here in our town
decisions.reason: Readable says what "here with us" means.

source.text: καὶ ἐσκανδαλίζοντο ἐν αὐτῷ.

records.literal_gloss: And they were taking offense at him.

en.L: And they took offense at {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: And they were offended by {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: So they were upset with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and would not accept {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: took offense: stumbled over him, so as to reject him
decisions.reason: The verb means to trip over something. They could not get past his ordinary family and so turned away from him (4:17, 14:27).

decisions.choice: were upset with him and would not accept him
decisions.reason: Readable spells out that taking offense here means rejecting him.

source.text: καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὅτι Οὐκ ἔστιν προφήτης ἄτιμος εἰ μὴ ἐν τῇ πατρίδι αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐν τοῖς συγγενεῦσιν αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And was saying to them Jesus, Not is a prophet without honor except in the hometown of him and among the relatives of him and in the household of him.

en.L: And Jesus said to them, "A prophet is not without honor except in his hometown and among his relatives and in his household."
en.B: Jesus told them, "Everywhere a prophet is honored, except in his own town, among his own kin, and in his own family."
en.R: Jesus said to them, "People everywhere honor a prophet, but not in the town where he grew up. Even his relatives and his own family do not honor him."

decisions.choice: a saying about prophets that Jesus applies to himself
decisions.reason: The words have the form of a proverb. By using it here, Jesus counts himself a prophet rejected by his own.

decisions.choice: household: his own family
decisions.reason: The list narrows from town to relatives to his own family, as in 3:21 and 3:31.

decisions.choice: said: an imperfect, he was saying
decisions.reason: Mark often uses this form for Jesus' sayings. It does not change the sense.

decisions.choice: everywhere a prophet is honored, except (B); people everywhere honor a prophet, but not (R)
alternatives: a prophet is not without honor except
decisions.reason: The double negative is turned into a positive statement, which says the same thing more plainly.

source.text: καὶ οὐκ ἐδύνατο ἐκεῖ ποιῆσαι οὐδεμίαν δύναμιν, εἰ μὴ ὀλίγοις ἀρρώστοις ἐπιθεὶς τὰς χεῖρας ἐθεράπευσεν·

records.literal_gloss: And not he was able there to do not any work of power, except on a few sick having laid the hands he healed;

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was not able to do any work of power there, except that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} laid [{{deity_pronoun:his|His}}] hands on a few sick [people and] healed [them];
en.B: There {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was not able to do any mighty work, apart from laying {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hands on a few who were sick and healing them.
en.R: Jesus was not able to do any powerful miracles there. The only thing {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did was to heal a few sick people by putting {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hands on them.

decisions.choice: not able: Mark links this with their unbelief (6:6)
decisions.reason: Mark says plainly that Jesus could not. In Mark, miracles answer faith (5:34). Where people would not trust him, they did not come to him, and his deeds would not have been signs to them. Mark does not explain further.

decisions.choice: laid his hands on: a touch to heal
decisions.reason: Jesus heals by touch elsewhere too (1:41; 5:23).

decisions.choice: except: the few healings are a small exception
decisions.reason: Even healing a few people is not counted as a work of power here, so few were they.

source.text: καὶ ἐθαύμαζεν διὰ τὴν ἀπιστίαν αὐτῶν.

records.literal_gloss: And he was marveling because of the unbelief of them.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was amazed because of their unbelief.
en.B: Their unbelief amazed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Jesus was amazed that they did not believe.

decisions.choice: unbelief: refusal to trust
decisions.reason: The word is the opposite of faith. It is set against the faith of the woman and of Jairus (5:34, 5:36).

decisions.choice: he was amazed: Jesus himself marvels
decisions.reason: Elsewhere in Mark the people marvel at Jesus. Here he marvels at them.

source.text: Καὶ περιῆγεν τὰς κώμας κύκλῳ διδάσκων.

records.literal_gloss: And he was going around the villages in a circle teaching.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was going around the villages in a circuit, teaching.
en.B: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went from village to village in that area, teaching.
en.R: Then Jesus went to the villages all around and taught the people there.

decisions.choice: he was going around teaching: a tour that went on for some time
decisions.reason: The imperfect tense and the participle describe ongoing work.

decisions.choice: in a circle: in the area around
decisions.reason: The word means round about. He visited the villages near Nazareth.

source.text: καὶ προσκαλεῖται τοὺς δώδεκα, καὶ ἤρξατο αὐτοὺς ἀποστέλλειν δύο δύο, καὶ ἐδίδου αὐτοῖς ἐξουσίαν τῶν πνευμάτων τῶν ἀκαθάρτων, καὶ παρήγγειλεν αὐτοῖς ἵνα μηδὲν αἴρωσιν εἰς ὁδὸν εἰ μὴ ῥάβδον μόνον, μὴ ἄρτον, μὴ πήραν, μὴ εἰς τὴν ζώνην χαλκόν, ἀλλὰ ὑποδεδεμένους σανδάλια, καὶ μὴ ἐνδύσησθε δύο χιτῶνας.

records.literal_gloss: And he calls to [him] the twelve, and began them to send out two [by] two, and was giving them authority over the spirits the unclean; \v 8 and he instructed them that nothing they should take for [the] road except a staff only, not bread, not bag, not in the belt copper, \v 9 but having been shod with sandals, and do not put on two tunics.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} calls the twelve to [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] and began to send them out two by two, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave them authority over the unclean spirits; \v 8 and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} instructed them to take nothing for the road except a staff only: no bread, no bag, no copper [money] in the belt, \v 9 but to wear sandals; and "Do not put on two tunics."
en.B: He called the Twelve to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and began sending them out in pairs, giving them authority over unclean spirits. \v 8 He told them to take nothing for the journey except a walking stick: no food, no traveler's bag, and no coins in their belts. \v 9 They were to wear sandals. "And do not put on a second tunic," {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said.
en.R: Jesus called the Twelve together. He began to send them out two at a time, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave them power over evil spirits. \v 8 He told them, "Take nothing with you for the trip except a walking stick. Do not take any food or a bag or any money. \v 9 Wear sandals, but do not take extra clothes."

decisions.choice: the twelve: the group Jesus appointed in 3:14-19
decisions.reason: Mark uses the number as the name of the group.

decisions.choice: two by two: in pairs
decisions.reason: Pairs could help each other, and two witnesses made a message stand (Deuteronomy 19:15).

decisions.choice: take nothing but a staff: they are to travel light and depend on the people who take them in
alternatives: they were to be poor forever
decisions.reason: No food, no bag for gifts, no money: they must rely on God and on hospitality (6:10). Sandals and a staff are what one needs to walk.

decisions.choice: bag: a traveler's bag for food or gifts; copper: small coins, carried in the belt
decisions.reason: A belt or sash was folded to hold coins.

decisions.choice: do not put on: the sentence moves from reported instructions to Jesus' own words
decisions.reason: Mark changes from "he instructed them that" to a direct command in the middle of the sentence.

decisions.choice: the Twelve
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable capitalize the number when it serves as the group's name. Literal keeps the plain word.

decisions.choice: direct speech throughout
alternatives: he instructed them that they should take nothing
decisions.reason: Readable gives all the instructions as Jesus' own words, since the Greek ends in direct speech.

source.text: καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· Ὅπου ἐὰν εἰσέλθητε εἰς οἰκίαν, ἐκεῖ μένετε ἕως ἂν ἐξέλθητε ἐκεῖθεν.

records.literal_gloss: And he was saying to them, Wherever you enter into a house, there remain until you go out from there.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Wherever you enter a house, stay there until you go out from there.
en.B: He told them, "When you go into a house, stay in it until you leave that town.
en.R: He said, "When someone lets you stay in their house, stay there until you leave that town.

decisions.choice: until you go out from there: until you leave the town
decisions.reason: "There" points to the place, not the house: they are to stay in one house for the whole visit.

decisions.choice: stay in one house: do not move around looking for better lodging
decisions.reason: The guest was to accept the first welcome given and not shame the host by leaving for a better offer.

decisions.choice: that town
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the place that "there" refers to.

source.text: καὶ ὃς ἂν τόπος μὴ δέξηται ὑμᾶς μηδὲ ἀκούσωσιν ὑμῶν, ἐκπορευόμενοι ἐκεῖθεν ἐκτινάξατε τὸν χοῦν τὸν ὑποκάτω τῶν ποδῶν ὑμῶν εἰς μαρτύριον αὐτοῖς.

records.literal_gloss: And whatever place not receives you nor they hear you, going out from there shake off the dust the [one] under the feet of you for a testimony to them.

en.L: And whatever place does not receive you, and they do not listen to you, as you go out from there, shake off the dust that is under your feet as a testimony to them."
en.B: Where people will not take you in or hear what you say, shake off the dust from under your feet as you go, as a witness against them."
en.R: If the people of a town will not take you in or listen to what you say, leave that town. As you go, shake the dust off your feet. That will be a warning to them."

decisions.choice: shake off the dust: a sign of breaking off ties with a place
decisions.reason: The act leaves the place to answer for itself. Paul and Barnabas do it in Acts 13:51.

decisions.choice: a testimony to them: a witness that will stand against them
decisions.reason: The act is a warning that they have heard and refused.

decisions.choice: the SBLGNT ends the saying here
alternatives: add: Truly I tell you, it will be more bearable for Sodom and Gomorrah on the day of judgment than for that town
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add the saying about Sodom and Gomorrah, as in Matthew 10:15. The earliest manuscripts lack it. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: place ... they: the people of that place
decisions.reason: The verb changes to plural because a place receives or listens through its people.

decisions.choice: people (B); the people in a town (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the people, as the plural verb does.

source.text: Καὶ ἐξελθόντες ἐκήρυξαν ἵνα μετανοῶσιν, καὶ δαιμόνια πολλὰ ἐξέβαλλον, καὶ ἤλειφον ἐλαίῳ πολλοὺς ἀρρώστους καὶ ἐθεράπευον.

records.literal_gloss: And having gone out they preached that they should repent, \v 13 and demons many they were casting out, and were anointing with oil many sick and were healing [them].

en.L: And they went out and proclaimed that [people] should repent, \v 13 and they were casting out many demons and anointing with oil many who were sick and healing [them].
en.B: So they went out and called people to repent. \v 13 They threw out demon after demon, and many who were sick they anointed with oil and made well.
en.R: So the Twelve went out. They told people to turn away from their sins and turn back to God. \v 13 They forced many demons to leave people. They put olive oil on many sick people and healed them.

decisions.choice: repent: turn from sin back to God
decisions.reason: The same message as John's and Jesus' (1:4, 1:15).

decisions.choice: anointing with oil: oil was used as a medicine and as a sign of God's care
decisions.reason: Olive oil was put on wounds and the sick (Luke 10:34). James 5:14 joins anointing with prayer for the sick.

decisions.choice: were casting out, anointing, healing: they did these things again and again
decisions.reason: The tenses describe repeated work through their mission.

decisions.choice: turn away from their sins and turn back to God
decisions.reason: Readable says what repenting means, as at 1:4.

decisions.choice: threw out (B); forced to leave people (R)
decisions.reason: The same words as at 1:34 and 3:15.

source.text: Καὶ ἤκουσεν ὁ βασιλεὺς Ἡρῴδης, φανερὸν γὰρ ἐγένετο τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἔλεγον ὅτι Ἰωάννης ὁ βαπτίζων ἐγήγερται ἐκ νεκρῶν, καὶ διὰ τοῦτο ἐνεργοῦσιν αἱ δυνάμεις ἐν αὐτῷ·

records.literal_gloss: And heard King Herod, for well known became the name of him, and they were saying, John the [one] baptizing has been raised from [the] dead, and because of this are at work the powers in him;

en.L: And King Herod heard [of it], for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name had become well known, and they were saying, "John the Baptizer has been raised from [the] dead, and because of this the powers are at work in him."
en.B: King Herod heard about it, for Jesus' name had become widely known. People were saying, "John the Baptizer has been raised from the dead. That is why these powers are at work in him."
en.R: King Herod heard about all this, because people everywhere now knew about Jesus. Some were saying, "John the Baptizer has come back from the dead! That is why he can do these miracles."

decisions.choice: King Herod: Herod Antipas, son of Herod the Great, ruler of Galilee and Perea
decisions.reason: Rome gave Antipas the lesser title tetrarch, ruler of part of a kingdom (Luke 3:1). Mark uses the title people gave him. Josephus records that Antipas later lost his land after seeking the title king.

decisions.choice: they were saying, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "he was saying", making this Herod's own opinion, as in 6:16. The SBLGNT reads the plural, which fits the list of opinions in 6:15. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: his name: Jesus' name
decisions.reason: The sentence follows the mission of the Twelve. The fame is Jesus', spread by their work.

decisions.choice: the powers are at work in him: miraculous powers act through him
decisions.reason: People think a prophet returned from the dead would have such powers.

decisions.choice: Jesus' name (B); knew about Jesus (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus, since the last person named is Herod.

source.text: ἄλλοι δὲ ἔλεγον ὅτι Ἠλίας ἐστίν· ἄλλοι δὲ ἔλεγον ὅτι προφήτης ὡς εἷς τῶν προφητῶν.

records.literal_gloss: Others but were saying, Elijah he is; others but were saying, A prophet like one of the prophets.

en.L: But others were saying, "He is Elijah." And others were saying, "[He is] a prophet, like one of the prophets."
en.B: Others said, "It is Elijah," and others again, "He is a prophet, one like the prophets of long ago."
en.R: Other people said, "He is Elijah, the prophet who was taken up to heaven long ago." Still others said, "He is a prophet like the great prophets of long ago."

decisions.choice: Elijah: the prophet God promised to send before the day of the Lord
decisions.reason: Malachi 4:5 promised that Elijah would come again. Elijah had not died but was taken up (2 Kings 2:11).

decisions.choice: like one of the prophets: a prophet of the old kind
alternatives: one of the old prophets come back to life
decisions.reason: These people do not say he is a prophet returned, only that he is like them.

decisions.choice: the prophet who was taken up to heaven long ago
decisions.reason: Readable explains who Elijah was.

source.text: ἀκούσας δὲ ὁ Ἡρῴδης ἔλεγεν· Ὃν ἐγὼ ἀπεκεφάλισα Ἰωάννην, οὗτος ἠγέρθη.

records.literal_gloss: Having heard but Herod was saying, Whom I beheaded, John, this one has been raised.

en.L: But when Herod heard [of it], he was saying, "John, whom I beheaded, this one has been raised."
en.B: But when Herod heard of it, he said, "It is John, the man I beheaded. He has been raised!"
en.R: But when Herod heard about it, he said, "It is John! I had his head cut off, but now he has come back to life!"

decisions.choice: I: emphatic, Herod knows he is to blame
decisions.reason: Herod adds the pronoun for emphasis: I myself had him killed.

decisions.choice: this one: Herod settles on one view
decisions.reason: Of the opinions in 6:14-15, Herod takes the first.

decisions.choice: had his head cut off
decisions.reason: Readable uses plain words, and "had" shows that Herod gave the order.

source.text: Αὐτὸς γὰρ ὁ Ἡρῴδης ἀποστείλας ἐκράτησεν τὸν Ἰωάννην καὶ ἔδησεν αὐτὸν ἐν φυλακῇ διὰ Ἡρῳδιάδα τὴν γυναῖκα Φιλίππου τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ αὐτοῦ, ὅτι αὐτὴν ἐγάμησεν·

records.literal_gloss: Himself for Herod having sent seized John and bound him in prison because of Herodias the wife of Philip the brother of him, because her he had married;

en.L: For Herod himself had sent and seized John and bound him in prison because of Herodias, the wife of Philip his brother, because he had married her;
en.B: It was Herod himself who had sent men to seize John and had tied him up in prison. He did it on account of Herodias, his brother Philip's wife, since he had married her.
en.R: Some time before this, Herod had sent soldiers to arrest John. They tied him up and put him in prison. Herod did this because of Herodias. She had been the wife of Herod's brother Philip, but Herod had married her.

decisions.choice: for: the story goes back to explain what happened to John earlier
decisions.reason: Mark tells John's death as a flashback, from 6:17 to 6:29.

decisions.choice: Herodias: Herod's niece, first married to his half-brother
decisions.reason: Josephus records that Herodias left her first husband, a half-brother of Antipas, to marry Antipas. He calls that brother Herod; Mark calls him Philip. The family used the name Herod for many of its men, and one man could have had both names.

decisions.choice: in prison: in one of Herod's fortresses
decisions.reason: Josephus says John was held at Machaerus, a fortress east of the Dead Sea.

decisions.choice: Some time before this
decisions.reason: Readable marks the flashback plainly.

source.text: ἔλεγεν γὰρ ὁ Ἰωάννης τῷ Ἡρῴδῃ ὅτι Οὐκ ἔξεστίν σοι ἔχειν τὴν γυναῖκα τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου.

records.literal_gloss: Was saying for John to Herod, Not it is lawful for you to have the wife of the brother of you.

en.L: For John had been saying to Herod, "It is not lawful for you to have your brother's wife."
en.B: John had kept telling Herod, "The law does not allow you to have your brother's wife."
en.R: John had told Herod again and again, "God's law says you must not marry your brother's wife."

decisions.choice: had been saying: John said it more than once
decisions.reason: The imperfect tense suggests a repeated rebuke.

decisions.choice: not lawful: the law of Moses forbade marrying a brother's wife while the brother lived
decisions.reason: Leviticus 18:16 and 20:21. The only exception was marrying a dead brother's childless widow (Deuteronomy 25:5), which this was not.

decisions.choice: the law does not allow (B); God's law says you must not (R)
decisions.reason: As at 3:4, Balanced and Readable say what "lawful" means.

source.text: ἡ δὲ Ἡρῳδιὰς ἐνεῖχεν αὐτῷ καὶ ἤθελεν αὐτὸν ἀποκτεῖναι, καὶ οὐκ ἠδύνατο·

records.literal_gloss: And Herodias was holding [it] against him and was wanting him to kill, and not was able;

en.L: And Herodias held a grudge against him and wanted to kill him, and she was not able;
en.B: So Herodias nursed a grudge against John and wanted him dead, but she could not bring it about,
en.R: So Herodias hated John and wanted him dead. But she had no way to do it,

decisions.choice: held it against him: kept a grudge
decisions.reason: The phrase means to hold on to anger against someone.

decisions.choice: wanted ... was not able: her wish was blocked for a time
decisions.reason: The next sentence gives the reason: Herod protected John.

source.text: ὁ γὰρ Ἡρῴδης ἐφοβεῖτο τὸν Ἰωάννην, εἰδὼς αὐτὸν ἄνδρα δίκαιον καὶ ἅγιον, καὶ συνετήρει αὐτόν, καὶ ἀκούσας αὐτοῦ πολλὰ ἠπόρει, καὶ ἡδέως αὐτοῦ ἤκουεν.

records.literal_gloss: for Herod was fearing John, knowing him [to be] a man righteous and holy, and was keeping safe him, and having heard him much he was perplexed, and gladly him was hearing.

en.L: for Herod feared John, knowing him [to be] a righteous and holy man, and he kept him safe. And when he heard him, he was greatly perplexed, and [yet] he heard him gladly.
en.B: because Herod stood in awe of John. He knew John was a righteous and holy man, so he kept him safe. Whenever he listened to John, he was left deeply troubled, and yet he liked to hear him.
en.R: because Herod was afraid of John. He knew that John was a holy man who did what was right, so he protected him. When Herod listened to John, he did not know what to think. But still he enjoyed listening to him.

decisions.choice: was greatly perplexed, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read "he did many things", meaning he acted on John's words. The older manuscripts read "he was greatly perplexed". Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: feared: held in awe, with some fear
decisions.reason: Herod respects John as a man of God and fears what might follow if he harms him.

decisions.choice: kept him safe: protected him from Herodias
decisions.reason: The verb means to guard or preserve. The sentence explains why Herodias could not kill him.

decisions.choice: perplexed, yet glad to listen: Herod is torn
decisions.reason: He is drawn to John's words and troubled by them at once.

decisions.choice: a holy man who did what was right
decisions.reason: Readable explains "righteous" in plain words.

source.text: Καὶ γενομένης ἡμέρας εὐκαίρου ὅτε Ἡρῴδης τοῖς γενεσίοις αὐτοῦ δεῖπνον ἐποίησεν τοῖς μεγιστᾶσιν αὐτοῦ καὶ τοῖς χιλιάρχοις καὶ τοῖς πρώτοις τῆς Γαλιλαίας, καὶ εἰσελθούσης τῆς θυγατρὸς αὐτῆς τῆς Ἡρῳδιάδος καὶ ὀρχησαμένης καὶ ἀρεσάσης τῷ Ἡρῴδῃ καὶ τοῖς συνανακειμένοις, εἶπεν ὁ βασιλεὺς τῷ κορασίῳ· Αἴτησόν με ὃ ἐὰν θέλῃς, καὶ δώσω σοι·

records.literal_gloss: And having come a day opportune, when Herod on the birthday of him a banquet made for the great men of him and the chiliarchs and the leading [men] of Galilee, \v 22 and having come in the daughter of herself Herodias and having danced and having pleased Herod and those reclining with [him], said the king to the girl, Ask me whatever you wish, and I will give to you;

en.L: And an opportune day came, when Herod on his birthday gave a banquet for his nobles and the military commanders and the leading [men] of Galilee, \v 22 and when the daughter of Herodias herself came in and danced, and pleased Herod and those reclining with [him], the king said to the girl, "Ask me whatever you wish, and I will give [it] to you."
en.B: At last Herodias had her chance. Herod held a feast on his birthday for the great men of his court, the officers of his army, and the chief men of Galilee. \v 22 Herodias's own daughter came in and danced, and Herod and those at table with him were delighted with her. So the king told the girl, "Name anything you like, and I will give it to you."
en.R: Then Herodias got her chance. It was Herod's birthday, and he gave a big dinner party. He invited his top officials, the commanders of his army, and the most important people in Galilee. \v 22 Herodias's daughter came in and danced for them. Herod and his guests liked her dancing very much. So King Herod said to the girl, "You can ask me for anything, and I will give it to you."

decisions.choice: an opportune day: the opportunity Herodias was waiting for
decisions.reason: The word means a convenient or fitting time. Coming after 6:19, it is her chance to act.

decisions.choice: the guests: court nobles, army commanders, and the chief men of Galilee
decisions.reason: The second word names officers over a thousand soldiers. Herod displays his power before all the leaders of his land.

decisions.choice: the daughter of Herodias herself, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Some important early manuscripts read "his daughter Herodias", which would make the girl Herod's own daughter, named Herodias. The SBLGNT text makes her the daughter of Herodias, which fits 6:24. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: the daughter: Josephus names Herodias's daughter Salome
decisions.reason: Mark does not give her name. Josephus says Herodias had a daughter, Salome, by her first husband.

decisions.choice: girl: a young girl, perhaps in her early teens
decisions.reason: The same word is used of Jairus' twelve-year-old daughter (5:41-42).

decisions.choice: At last Herodias had her chance (B); Then Herodias got her chance (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say for whom the day was opportune, as the meaning note explains.

source.text: καὶ ὤμοσεν αὐτῇ· Ὅ τι ἐάν με αἰτήσῃς δώσω σοι ἕως ἡμίσους τῆς βασιλείας μου.

records.literal_gloss: And he swore to her, Whatever me you ask I will give you, up to half of the kingdom of me.

en.L: And he swore to her, "Whatever you ask me, I will give you, up to half of my kingdom."
en.B: He even swore an oath to her: "Anything you ask me for, I will give you, as much as half my kingdom."
en.R: He made a solemn promise to her: "I will give you anything you ask for, even half of my kingdom!"

decisions.choice: up to half of my kingdom: the words of King Ahasuerus to Esther
decisions.reason: The Persian king says the same to Esther (Esther 5:3, 5:6, 7:2).

decisions.choice: half my kingdom: a boast of how generous he will be
decisions.reason: Herod could not give away land; Rome held power over his realm. The words show a lavish promise made in front of guests.

decisions.choice: swore: made a binding oath
decisions.reason: The oath binds him before his guests (6:26).

source.text: καὶ ἐξελθοῦσα εἶπεν τῇ μητρὶ αὐτῆς· Τί αἰτήσωμαι;

records.literal_gloss: And having gone out she said to the mother of her, What shall I ask for?

en.L: And she went out and said to her mother, "What shall I ask for?"
en.B: The girl went out to her mother and said, "What should I ask for?"
en.R: The girl left the room and asked her mother, "What should I ask him for?"

decisions.choice: went out: Herodias is not at the banquet
decisions.reason: Men and women ate apart at such feasts. The girl leaves the hall to ask her mother.

decisions.choice: ask for: a form meaning to ask for oneself
alternatives: ask on behalf of someone else
decisions.reason: The girl asks what she should request for herself.

source.text: ἡ δὲ εἶπεν· Τὴν κεφαλὴν Ἰωάννου τοῦ βαπτίζοντος.

records.literal_gloss: And she said, The head of John the [one] baptizing.

en.L: And she said, "The head of John the Baptizer."
en.B: "The head of John the Baptizer," her mother answered.
en.R: Her mother answered, "Ask for the head of John the Baptizer."

decisions.choice: she said: the mother, Herodias
decisions.reason: The article marks a change of speaker.

decisions.choice: the one baptizing: the title Mark uses at 1:4 and 6:14
alternatives: a description of what John was doing then
decisions.reason: The participle serves as a title.

decisions.choice: Ask for
decisions.reason: Readable makes the answer a full sentence.

source.text: καὶ εἰσελθοῦσα εὐθὺς μετὰ σπουδῆς πρὸς τὸν βασιλέα ᾐτήσατο λέγουσα· Θέλω ἵνα ἐξαυτῆς δῷς μοι ἐπὶ πίνακι τὴν κεφαλὴν Ἰωάννου τοῦ βαπτιστοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And having entered immediately with haste to the king she asked, saying, I want that at once you give to me on a platter the head of John the Baptist.

en.L: And immediately she came in with haste to the king and asked, saying, "I want you to give me at once on a platter the head of John the Baptist."
en.B: Straight away she rushed back to the king and made her request. "I want the head of John the Baptist," she said, "on a platter, and I want it now."
en.R: The girl hurried back in to the king. "Give me John the Baptist's head on a big plate," she said. "I want it right now!"

decisions.choice: the Baptist: here a noun, the title used also in Matthew and Luke
decisions.reason: Mark uses "the one who baptizes" at 1:4, 6:14 and 6:24, and the noun here and at 8:28. Both name the same man.

decisions.choice: immediately, with haste, at once: she will not give Herod time to change his mind
decisions.reason: Three words of speed press the demand on the king.

decisions.choice: platter: a large dish from the banquet table
decisions.reason: The head is to be served like a course of the meal.

decisions.choice: the Baptist
decisions.reason: Here Mark uses the noun, not the participle of 1:4, 6:14 and 6:24, so the levels say "the Baptist" and keep the difference the meaning note describes.

decisions.choice: a big plate
decisions.reason: Readable uses the plainer word.

source.text: καὶ περίλυπος γενόμενος ὁ βασιλεὺς διὰ τοὺς ὅρκους καὶ τοὺς ἀνακειμένους οὐκ ἠθέλησεν ἀθετῆσαι αὐτήν·

records.literal_gloss: And very sorrowful having become the king, because of the oaths and those reclining, not he wanted to refuse her;

en.L: And though the king became very sorrowful, because of the oaths and those reclining [at table] he did not want to refuse her;
en.B: This grieved the king deeply. Yet he had sworn oaths in front of his guests, and he was not willing to break his word to her.
en.R: The king was very upset. But he had made a promise in front of all his guests. So he did not want to say no to her.

decisions.choice: very sorrowful: deeply grieved
decisions.reason: The same strong word Jesus uses of himself in Gethsemane (14:34).

decisions.choice: the oaths and the guests: to break a public oath would shame him
decisions.reason: Herod cares more for his standing before his guests than for John's life.

decisions.choice: refuse: set aside, break faith with
decisions.reason: The verb means to cancel or go back on a promise.

decisions.choice: break his word to her
decisions.reason: Balanced brings out the sense of breaking a promise.

source.text: καὶ εὐθὺς ἀποστείλας ὁ βασιλεὺς σπεκουλάτορα ἐπέταξεν ἐνέγκαι τὴν κεφαλὴν αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And immediately having sent the king an executioner, he commanded to bring the head of him.

en.L: And immediately the king sent an executioner and commanded [him] to bring his head.
en.B: At once the king sent one of his guards with orders to bring John's head.
en.R: Right away the king sent a soldier from his guard and ordered him to bring John's head.

decisions.choice: executioner: a soldier of the guard, who also carried out executions
decisions.reason: The word is a Latin loanword for a scout or bodyguard. Such guards carried out death sentences.

decisions.choice: immediately: Herod acts at once
decisions.reason: The haste of the girl is met by the haste of the king.

decisions.choice: John's head
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name John, since the last man named is the king.

source.text: καὶ ἀπελθὼν ἀπεκεφάλισεν αὐτὸν ἐν τῇ φυλακῇ καὶ ἤνεγκεν τὴν κεφαλὴν αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ πίνακι καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτὴν τῷ κορασίῳ, καὶ τὸ κοράσιον ἔδωκεν αὐτὴν τῇ μητρὶ αὐτῆς.

records.literal_gloss: And having gone he beheaded him in the prison \v 28 and brought the head of him on a platter and gave it to the girl, and the girl gave it to the mother of her.

en.L: And he went and beheaded him in the prison \v 28 and brought his head on a platter and gave it to the girl, and the girl gave it to her mother.
en.B: The man went and beheaded John in the prison. \v 28 He carried the head in on a platter and handed it to the girl, and she handed it to her mother.
en.R: The soldier went to the prison and cut off John's head. \v 28 He brought it back on a plate and gave it to the girl. Then the girl gave it to her mother.

decisions.choice: the girl gave it to her mother: the head reaches the one who wanted it
decisions.reason: The story ends with Herodias, who planned John's death (6:19).

decisions.choice: beheaded him: John dies as a prophet at the hands of a ruler
decisions.reason: John's death foreshadows Jesus' own death at the hands of rulers (9:13; 15:15).

decisions.choice: John (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name John to make clear who was killed.

source.text: καὶ ἀκούσαντες οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἦλθον καὶ ἦραν τὸ πτῶμα αὐτοῦ καὶ ἔθηκαν αὐτὸ ἐν μνημείῳ.

records.literal_gloss: And having heard [it], the disciples of him came and took up the corpse of him and laid it in a tomb.

en.L: And when his disciples heard [of it], they came and took up his corpse and laid it in a tomb.
en.B: When John's disciples heard about it, they came for his body and buried it in a tomb.
en.R: When John's followers heard what had happened, they came and took his body away. They buried it in a tomb.

decisions.choice: his disciples: John's disciples
decisions.reason: John had followers of his own (2:18).

decisions.choice: corpse: a dead body
decisions.reason: The word is used of the dead. Joseph of Arimathea will do the same for Jesus (15:45-46).

decisions.choice: John's
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name whose disciples they were.

source.text: Καὶ συνάγονται οἱ ἀπόστολοι πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν, καὶ ἀπήγγειλαν αὐτῷ πάντα ὅσα ἐποίησαν καὶ ὅσα ἐδίδαξαν.

records.literal_gloss: And are gathered together the apostles to Jesus, and they reported to him all things whatever they did and whatever they taught.

en.L: And the apostles gather together to Jesus, and they reported to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} all that they had done and all that they had taught.
en.B: The apostles returned to Jesus and gave {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} a report of all they had done and all they had taught.
en.R: The apostles came back to Jesus. They told {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} about everything they had done and taught.

decisions.choice: apostles: those sent out, here the Twelve back from their mission
decisions.reason: The word means ones who are sent. Mark uses it only here, after Jesus sent them (6:7).

decisions.choice: gather: present tense in a story about the past
decisions.reason: As in 6:1, the present is vivid; the sense is past.

decisions.choice: done and taught: deeds come first
decisions.reason: Their report covers their healing and casting out (6:13) and their preaching (6:12).

source.text: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Δεῦτε ὑμεῖς αὐτοὶ κατ’ ἰδίαν εἰς ἔρημον τόπον καὶ ἀναπαύσασθε ὀλίγον.

records.literal_gloss: And he says to them, Come you yourselves by own [self] to a deserted place and rest a little.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to them, "Come, you yourselves, by yourselves to a deserted place and rest a little."
en.B: He said to them, "Come away on your own, to a place without people, and get a little rest."
en.R: Jesus said to them, "Come with me. Let us go to a quiet place where we can be alone. You need to rest for a while."

decisions.choice: deserted place: a lonely place without towns, the same word as wilderness
decisions.reason: Mark uses the word for the wilderness of John's work and of Jesus' prayer (1:3-4, 1:35, 1:45).

decisions.choice: you yourselves, by yourselves: away from the crowds
decisions.reason: Jesus goes with them (6:32). The point is to be apart from the crowds.

decisions.choice: Come with me. Let us go ... where we can be alone.
decisions.reason: Readable shows that Jesus went too, as 6:32 says.

source.text: ἦσαν γὰρ οἱ ἐρχόμενοι καὶ οἱ ὑπάγοντες πολλοί, καὶ οὐδὲ φαγεῖν εὐκαίρουν.

records.literal_gloss: Were for those coming and those going many, and not even to eat they had opportunity.

en.L: For those coming and those going were many, and they did not even have opportunity to eat.
en.B: There was a constant stream of people arriving and leaving, and they could not even find time for a meal.
en.R: Crowds of people kept coming and going. Jesus and the apostles did not even have time to eat.

decisions.choice: those coming and those going: a steady flow of people
decisions.reason: The phrase pictures people always arriving and leaving.

decisions.choice: they: Jesus and the apostles
decisions.reason: As in 3:20, the crowd leaves them no time even to eat.

decisions.choice: Jesus and the apostles
decisions.reason: Readable names who had no time to eat.

source.text: καὶ ἀπῆλθον ἐν τῷ πλοίῳ εἰς ἔρημον τόπον κατ’ ἰδίαν.

records.literal_gloss: And they went away in the boat to a deserted place by own [self].

en.L: And they went away in the boat to a deserted place by themselves.
en.B: So they left in the boat, alone, for a remote spot.
en.R: So they got into the boat and went off alone to a quiet place.

decisions.choice: in the boat: the boat kept ready for Jesus (3:9; 4:36)
decisions.reason: The article points to the boat already in the story.

decisions.choice: deserted place: a place without towns
decisions.reason: The same words as in 6:31.

source.text: καὶ εἶδον αὐτοὺς ὑπάγοντας καὶ ἐπέγνωσαν πολλοί, καὶ πεζῇ ἀπὸ πασῶν τῶν πόλεων συνέδραμον ἐκεῖ καὶ προῆλθον αὐτούς.

records.literal_gloss: And saw them going and recognized [them] many, and on foot from all the towns they ran together there and went ahead of them.

en.L: And many saw them going and recognized [them], and on foot from all the towns they ran together there and arrived ahead of them.
en.B: But many people saw them leaving and knew who they were. People from all the towns hurried there on foot and reached the place before them.
en.R: But many people saw them leaving and knew who they were. People from all the nearby towns ran there along the shore. They got to the place before Jesus and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} apostles did.

decisions.choice: on foot: by land, around the shore
decisions.reason: The crowd goes by land while the boat goes by water.

decisions.choice: and went ahead of them, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: add: and came together to him
decisions.reason: Later manuscripts expand the end of the verse in several ways. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: recognized: knew who they were
decisions.reason: The verb means to recognize someone.

decisions.choice: along the shore
decisions.reason: Readable shows how the crowd could get there first.

source.text: καὶ ἐξελθὼν εἶδεν πολὺν ὄχλον, καὶ ἐσπλαγχνίσθη ἐπ’ αὐτοὺς ὅτι ἦσαν ὡς πρόβατα μὴ ἔχοντα ποιμένα, καὶ ἤρξατο διδάσκειν αὐτοὺς πολλά.

records.literal_gloss: And having gone out he saw a great crowd, and was moved with compassion toward them, because they were like sheep not having a shepherd, and he began to teach them many things.

en.L: And when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went out, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw a great crowd, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had compassion on them, because they were like sheep not having a shepherd, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} began to teach them many things.
en.B: When Jesus came ashore, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw a great crowd. He felt deep pity for them, for they were like sheep with no shepherd, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} began to teach them at length.
en.R: When Jesus got out of the boat, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw a large crowd. He felt sorry for them, because they were like sheep that have no shepherd to take care of them. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} began to teach them many things.

decisions.choice: sheep without a shepherd: God's people without a leader
decisions.reason: Moses asked God for a leader so that Israel would not be like sheep without a shepherd (Numbers 27:17; see 1 Kings 22:17; Ezekiel 34:5). In Ezekiel 34 God promises to shepherd his people himself.

decisions.choice: had compassion: was moved deep inside
alternatives: felt sorry in a distant way
decisions.reason: The verb comes from the word for the inward parts, the seat of feeling.

decisions.choice: went out: from the boat
decisions.reason: He comes ashore at the place where the crowd waits.

decisions.choice: he began to teach them: the shepherd first feeds them with teaching
decisions.reason: Teaching comes before the meal. Both are a shepherd's care.

decisions.choice: to take care of them
decisions.reason: Readable says what a shepherd does.

source.text: Καὶ ἤδη ὥρας πολλῆς γενομένης προσελθόντες αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἔλεγον ὅτι Ἔρημός ἐστιν ὁ τόπος, καὶ ἤδη ὥρα πολλή·

records.literal_gloss: And already [the] hour much having become, having come to him the disciples of him were saying, Deserted is the place, and already [the] hour [is] much;

en.L: And when the hour had already become late, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and were saying, "The place is deserted, and the hour [is] already late;
en.B: By now it was late in the day, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and said, "No one lives out here, and it is getting late.
en.R: Late in the afternoon, Jesus' followers came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They said, "No one lives near this place, and it is already late.

decisions.choice: the hour much: late in the day
decisions.reason: The phrase means the day was far gone. The meal comes before nightfall (6:47).

decisions.choice: deserted: without towns or food
decisions.reason: The same word as "deserted place" in 6:31-32.

decisions.choice: late in the afternoon
decisions.reason: Readable gives the time of day in plain words.

source.text: ἀπόλυσον αὐτούς, ἵνα ἀπελθόντες εἰς τοὺς κύκλῳ ἀγροὺς καὶ κώμας ἀγοράσωσιν ἑαυτοῖς τί φάγωσιν.

records.literal_gloss: Send away them, so that having gone into the surrounding fields and villages they may buy for themselves something they may eat.

en.L: Dismiss them, so that they may go into the surrounding countryside and villages and buy themselves something to eat."
en.B: Send the people away, so they can go to the farms and villages round about and get themselves some food."
en.R: Tell the people to go away now. Then they can go to the farms and villages near here and buy some food for themselves."

decisions.choice: fields: farms and country places
decisions.reason: The word means the countryside with its farms.

decisions.choice: send them away: the disciples see no other answer
decisions.reason: They mean to help the crowd. Jesus answers with another way (6:37).

source.text: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Δότε αὐτοῖς ὑμεῖς φαγεῖν.

records.literal_gloss: But answering he said to them, Give them you to eat.

en.L: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} answered and said to them, "You give them [something] to eat."
en.B: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} replied, "You yourselves give them something to eat."
en.R: But Jesus answered, "You give them something to eat."

decisions.choice: you: emphatic
decisions.reason: Jesus puts the task on the disciples themselves.

decisions.choice: give them to eat: the words of Elisha to his servant
decisions.reason: Elisha says the same when he feeds a hundred men with twenty loaves (2 Kings 4:42-44).

source.text: καὶ λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Ἀπελθόντες ἀγοράσωμεν δηναρίων διακοσίων ἄρτους καὶ δώσομεν αὐτοῖς φαγεῖν;

records.literal_gloss: And they say to him, Having gone shall we buy of denarii two hundred loaves and shall give them to eat?

en.L: And they say to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Shall we go and buy 200 denarii [worth] of bread and give [it] to them to eat?"
en.B: They said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Are we to go and spend {{units:eight months' wages|200 denarii}} on bread and give it to them to eat?"
en.R: The followers said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} want us to go and spend {{units:eight months' pay|200 denarii}} on bread to feed them?"

decisions.choice: 200 denarii: a large sum, about eight months' pay for a laborer
decisions.reason: A denarius was a Roman silver coin, a day's wage for a farm worker (Matthew 20:2). Two hundred days of work, with no work on the Sabbath, comes to about eight months.

decisions.choice: a question that shows disbelief
decisions.reason: The disciples think the idea is impossible.

decisions.choice: they say: present tense in a story about the past
decisions.reason: As in 6:1, the sense is past.

decisions.choice: eight months' wages (B); eight months' pay (R); 200 denarii as the original unit
decisions.reason: The units setting gives a modern sense of the sum by default and the coin name as the alternative. Literal keeps the coin.

source.text: ὁ δὲ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Πόσους ἔχετε ἄρτους;

records.literal_gloss: And he says to them, How many have you loaves?

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to them, "How many loaves do you have?
en.B: He asked them, "How many loaves do you have?
en.R: Jesus asked them, "How many loaves of bread do you have?

decisions.choice: loaves: small, flat, round loaves
decisions.reason: Bread was baked in small flat cakes, of barley or wheat. Each was a meal for one.

decisions.choice: he says: present tense in a story about the past
decisions.reason: As in 6:1, the sense is past.

source.text: ὑπάγετε ἴδετε.

records.literal_gloss: Go, see.

en.L: Go [and] see."
en.B: Go and look."
en.R: Go and find out."

decisions.choice: go, see: two short commands without a link
decisions.reason: The commands are brisk.

source.text: καὶ γνόντες λέγουσιν· Πέντε, καὶ δύο ἰχθύας.

records.literal_gloss: And having found out they say, Five, and two fish.

en.L: And when they had found out, they say, "Five, and two fish."
en.B: When they had found out, they told {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Five, and two fish."
en.R: They found out and came back. "We have five loaves of bread and two fish," they said.

decisions.choice: five: five loaves
decisions.reason: The answer repeats the word loaves from the question.

decisions.choice: fish: likely dried or salted fish eaten with bread
decisions.reason: Fish from the lake was salted and dried and eaten with bread.

decisions.choice: We have five loaves of bread
decisions.reason: Readable makes the answer a full sentence.

source.text: καὶ ἐπέταξεν αὐτοῖς ἀνακλῖναι πάντας συμπόσια συμπόσια ἐπὶ τῷ χλωρῷ χόρτῳ.

records.literal_gloss: And he commanded them to recline all, companies [by] companies, on the green grass.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} commanded them [to make] all recline, company by company, on the green grass.
en.B: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} ordered them to seat all the people on the green grass in companies, as at a meal.
en.R: Then Jesus told the apostles to have all the people sit down on the green grass in groups.

decisions.choice: recline in companies: sit in groups as guests at a meal
decisions.reason: The verb is used for taking a place at a meal. The repeated word means party by party, like guests at a dinner.

decisions.choice: green grass: it is spring, and the scene recalls the shepherd who makes his flock lie down in green pastures
decisions.reason: Grass is green in Galilee in spring, near Passover. Psalm 23:2 pictures the Lord as a shepherd who makes his sheep lie down in green pastures, after 6:34.

decisions.choice: commanded them: he tells the disciples to seat everyone
decisions.reason: The infinitive can mean he told them to sit or told the disciples to seat them. The disciples serve the crowd in 6:41.

decisions.choice: the apostles
decisions.reason: Readable names whom he told.

source.text: καὶ ἀνέπεσαν πρασιαὶ πρασιαὶ κατὰ ἑκατὸν καὶ κατὰ πεντήκοντα.

records.literal_gloss: And they reclined, plots [by] plots, by hundred and by fifty.

en.L: And they reclined in rows, plot by plot, by hundreds and by fifties.
en.B: So they sat down in groups like the plots of a garden, in hundreds and in fifties.
en.R: So the people sat down in groups. Some groups had 100 people, and some had fifty.

decisions.choice: plots: garden beds, a picture of neat groups
decisions.reason: The word means a garden bed. The groups on the grass looked like rows of plants.

decisions.choice: hundreds and fifties: like Israel ordered in the wilderness
decisions.reason: Moses set leaders over thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens (Exodus 18:21, 18:25).

decisions.choice: like the plots of a garden
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture as a simile.

source.text: καὶ λαβὼν τοὺς πέντε ἄρτους καὶ τοὺς δύο ἰχθύας ἀναβλέψας εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν εὐλόγησεν καὶ κατέκλασεν τοὺς ἄρτους καὶ ἐδίδου τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ ἵνα παρατιθῶσιν αὐτοῖς, καὶ τοὺς δύο ἰχθύας ἐμέρισεν πᾶσιν.

records.literal_gloss: And having taken the five loaves and the two fish, having looked up to the heaven he blessed and broke the loaves and was giving to the disciples so that they might set before them, and the two fish he divided among all.

en.L: And taking the five loaves and the two fish, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} looked up to heaven and blessed, and broke the loaves and kept giving [them] to the disciples to set before them, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} divided the two fish among all.
en.B: Jesus took the five loaves and two fish, looked up to heaven, and spoke a blessing. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} broke the loaves and handed them again and again to the disciples to serve to the people. And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} shared out the two fish among everyone.
en.R: Jesus took the five loaves of bread and the two fish. He looked up to heaven and thanked God for the food. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} broke the loaves into pieces and kept giving them to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers. They passed them out to the people. He also divided the two fish so that everyone had some.

decisions.choice: blessed: praised God over the food
alternatives: blessed the bread to change it
decisions.reason: A Jewish meal began with a blessing of God, who gives bread. The verb has no object here.

decisions.choice: took, blessed, broke, gave: the same actions as at the Last Supper
decisions.reason: Mark uses the same four verbs at 14:22.

decisions.choice: kept giving: the bread kept coming from his hands
decisions.reason: The imperfect tense pictures him handing out bread again and again.

decisions.choice: the disciples: the SBLGNT has no "his"
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "his disciples". The meaning is the same. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: thanked God for the food
decisions.reason: Readable says whom the blessing addressed.

source.text: καὶ ἔφαγον πάντες καὶ ἐχορτάσθησαν·

records.literal_gloss: And ate all and were satisfied.

en.L: And all ate and were satisfied.
en.B: They all ate until they were full.
en.R: Everyone ate as much as they wanted.

decisions.choice: were satisfied: filled, with nothing lacking
decisions.reason: The verb is used for feeding animals until full, and for people eating their fill.

decisions.choice: all ate and were satisfied: God feeding his people in the wilderness
decisions.reason: God fed Israel with manna in the wilderness (Exodus 16), and Psalm 78:29 says they ate and were well filled.

source.text: καὶ ἦραν κλάσματα δώδεκα κοφίνων πληρώματα καὶ ἀπὸ τῶν ἰχθύων.

records.literal_gloss: And they took up broken pieces, of twelve baskets fullnesses, and from the fish.

en.L: And they took up broken pieces, the fill of twelve baskets, and [some] of the fish.
en.B: Then they gathered up twelve baskets full of broken pieces of bread, and of the fish too.
en.R: Afterward they picked up the pieces of bread and fish that were left. There was enough to fill twelve baskets.

decisions.choice: baskets: wicker baskets, the kind carried by travelers
decisions.reason: A different word is used for the larger baskets in 8:8.

decisions.choice: twelve baskets: more left over than there was at the start
decisions.reason: The number may recall the twelve tribes or the twelve apostles; Mark does not explain it.

decisions.choice: they: most likely the disciples
decisions.reason: The disciples served the food, and it is natural that they gathered what was left.

source.text: καὶ ἦσαν οἱ φαγόντες τοὺς ἄρτους πεντακισχίλιοι ἄνδρες.

records.literal_gloss: And were those having eaten the loaves five thousand men.

en.L: And those who ate the loaves were 5,000 men.
en.B: The men who had eaten the loaves numbered 5,000.
en.R: There were 5,000 men who ate the bread.

decisions.choice: men: adult males
decisions.reason: The word means men as distinct from women and children. Mark counts the men; Matthew 14:21 says women and children ate as well.

decisions.choice: the loaves, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Some important manuscripts do not have "the loaves". The sense is the same. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.
Numbers above ninety-nine are written as numerals. "Men" takes no gender setting, because only males are meant.

source.text: Καὶ εὐθὺς ἠνάγκασεν τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ ἐμβῆναι εἰς τὸ πλοῖον καὶ προάγειν εἰς τὸ πέραν πρὸς Βηθσαϊδάν, ἕως αὐτὸς ἀπολύει τὸν ὄχλον.

records.literal_gloss: And immediately he compelled the disciples of him to embark into the boat and to go ahead to the other side to Bethsaida, while he himself dismisses the crowd.

en.L: And immediately {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples get into the boat and go ahead to the other side, to Bethsaida, while {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} dismisses the crowd.
en.B: Right away Jesus pressed {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples to board the boat and cross ahead of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to Bethsaida on the other side, while {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} dismissed the crowd.
en.R: Right after that, Jesus told {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers to get into the boat and go ahead of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} across the lake to the town of Bethsaida. He stayed behind to send the people home.

decisions.choice: compelled: urged strongly, made them go
decisions.reason: The verb means to force or press. Mark does not say why. John 6:15 tells that the crowd wanted to make Jesus king.

decisions.choice: Bethsaida: a town on the north shore, east of where the Jordan enters the lake
alternatives: a town on the west shore
decisions.reason: The boat in fact lands at Gennesaret, on the west shore (6:53). The wind may have turned them back (6:48). Bethsaida is reached in 8:22.

decisions.choice: dismisses: a present tense, while he sends the crowd away
decisions.reason: He stays to send the crowd home while the disciples go.

decisions.choice: the town of
decisions.reason: Readable says that Bethsaida was a town.

source.text: καὶ ἀποταξάμενος αὐτοῖς ἀπῆλθεν εἰς τὸ ὄρος προσεύξασθαι.

records.literal_gloss: And having taken leave of them he departed to the mountain to pray.

en.L: And after taking leave of them, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went away to the mountain to pray.
en.B: After saying goodbye to them, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went off up the mountain to pray.
en.R: After {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said goodbye to the people, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went up into the hills to pray.

decisions.choice: them: the crowd, most likely
decisions.reason: The last group mentioned is the crowd. The disciples had already left (6:45).

decisions.choice: to pray: Jesus prays alone at turning points
decisions.reason: Mark shows him praying alone at 1:35 and in Gethsemane (14:32-39).

decisions.choice: the mountain: the hills above the lake
decisions.reason: The word can mean the hill country.

decisions.choice: the people
decisions.reason: Readable names who "them" are, following the meaning note.

source.text: Καὶ ὀψίας γενομένης ἦν τὸ πλοῖον ἐν μέσῳ τῆς θαλάσσης, καὶ αὐτὸς μόνος ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς.

records.literal_gloss: And evening having come, was the boat in [the] middle of the sea, and he alone on the land.

en.L: And when evening came, the boat was in the middle of the sea, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} [was] alone on the land.
en.B: When evening came, the boat was far out on the lake, and Jesus was alone on land.
en.R: When it was evening, the boat was out in the middle of Lake Galilee. Jesus was alone on the shore.

decisions.choice: evening: after sunset, the start of the night
decisions.reason: The meal took place late in the day (6:35); now night has come.

decisions.choice: in the middle of the sea: far from land
decisions.reason: The phrase means well out on the water.

decisions.choice: the lake (B); Lake Galilee (R)
decisions.reason: As in chapters 1 to 5.

source.text: καὶ ἰδὼν αὐτοὺς βασανιζομένους ἐν τῷ ἐλαύνειν, ἦν γὰρ ὁ ἄνεμος ἐναντίος αὐτοῖς, περὶ τετάρτην φυλακὴν τῆς νυκτὸς ἔρχεται πρὸς αὐτοὺς περιπατῶν ἐπὶ τῆς θαλάσσης· καὶ ἤθελεν παρελθεῖν αὐτούς.

records.literal_gloss: And having seen them straining in the rowing, was for the wind against them, about [the] fourth watch of the night he comes to them walking on the sea; and he was wanting to pass by them.

en.L: And seeing them straining in the rowing, for the wind was against them, about the fourth watch of the night {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} comes to them, walking on the sea; and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wanted to pass by them.
en.B: He saw them struggling at the oars, since the wind was against them. Toward the end of the night, in the fourth watch, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came out to them walking on the lake. He meant to pass by them.
en.R: Jesus saw that {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers were working very hard to row the boat, because the wind was blowing against them. Sometime between three and six o'clock in the morning, Jesus came to them. He was walking on top of the water! He was going to go on past them.

decisions.choice: the fourth watch of the night: from about three to six in the morning
decisions.reason: The Romans divided the night into four watches. The disciples have rowed most of the night.

decisions.choice: he wanted to pass by them: as God passed by Moses and Elijah to show himself
alternatives: he meant to walk ahead of them
decisions.reason: God passed by Moses to show his glory (Exodus 33:19-22; 34:6) and passed by Elijah on the mountain (1 Kings 19:11). The words most likely mean Jesus meant to show himself to them, not to leave them. Some read it simply as walking past.

decisions.choice: walking on the sea: what scripture says God alone does
decisions.reason: Job 9:8 says God alone treads on the waves of the sea (see Psalm 77:19).

decisions.choice: straining: tormented, struggling hard
decisions.reason: The word means to be tormented; here, worn out by rowing against the wind.

decisions.choice: toward the end of the night, in the fourth watch (B); sometime between three and six o'clock in the morning (R)
alternatives: about the fourth watch of the night
decisions.reason: Balanced shows where the watch falls in the night; Readable gives the time in modern terms.

source.text: οἱ δὲ ἰδόντες αὐτὸν ἐπὶ τῆς θαλάσσης περιπατοῦντα ἔδοξαν ὅτι φάντασμά ἐστιν καὶ ἀνέκραξαν, πάντες γὰρ αὐτὸν εἶδον καὶ ἐταράχθησαν.

records.literal_gloss: And having seen him on the sea walking they thought that a ghost it is, and cried out; \v 50 all for him saw and were troubled.

en.L: But when they saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} walking on the sea, they thought that it was a ghost, and they cried out, \v 50 for they all saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and were terrified.
en.B: When they saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} walking on the lake, they took {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} for a ghost and cried out in fear, \v 50 for every one of them saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and they were shaken.
en.R: The followers saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} walking on the water. They thought {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was a ghost, and they screamed. \v 50 All of them saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and they were very frightened.

decisions.choice: ghost: an apparition, a phantom
decisions.reason: The word means something that appears but is not real.

decisions.choice: for they all saw him: it was not one man's imagination
decisions.reason: Mark explains why they all cried out.

decisions.choice: terrified: shaken, thrown into fear
decisions.reason: The verb means to be stirred up or deeply disturbed.

source.text: ὁ δὲ εὐθὺς ἐλάλησεν μετ’ αὐτῶν, καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Θαρσεῖτε, ἐγώ εἰμι, μὴ φοβεῖσθε.

records.literal_gloss: But he immediately spoke with them, and says to them, Take courage, I am, do not fear.

en.L: But immediately {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke with them and says to them, "Take courage; I am [he]; do not be afraid."
en.B: But right away {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke to them. "Be brave," {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said. "It is I. Stop being afraid."
en.R: Right away Jesus spoke to them. "Cheer up!" {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said. "It is I, Jesus. Do not be afraid."

decisions.choice: I am: he tells them who he is, in words that echo the name God gave himself
alternatives: only: it is me, a simple greeting
decisions.reason: In ordinary speech the words mean "it is I". But God spoke of himself as "I am" (Exodus 3:14), and in Isaiah God says "I am he" and tells his people not to fear (Isaiah 43:10; 51:12). Coming from one who walks on the sea, the words most likely carry both senses. Jesus uses them again in 14:62.

decisions.choice: take courage: be brave, do not lose heart
decisions.reason: The verb means to be confident or bold.

decisions.choice: do not be afraid: stop being afraid
decisions.reason: The present tense with "not" usually tells someone to stop what they are already doing.

decisions.choice: It is I, Jesus.
decisions.reason: Readable adds the name so that the plain sense is clear. The meaning note gives the deeper sense.

source.text: καὶ ἀνέβη πρὸς αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸ πλοῖον, καὶ ἐκόπασεν ὁ ἄνεμος.

records.literal_gloss: And he went up to them into the boat, and ceased the wind.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went up to them into the boat, and the wind ceased.
en.B: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} got into the boat beside them, and the wind dropped.
en.R: Jesus climbed into their boat. The wind stopped.

decisions.choice: ceased: grew tired, died down
decisions.reason: The same verb as at 4:39.

decisions.choice: the wind stops when he comes into the boat
decisions.reason: As in 4:39, the storm obeys him.

source.text: καὶ λίαν ἐκ περισσοῦ ἐν ἑαυτοῖς ἐξίσταντο, οὐ γὰρ συνῆκαν ἐπὶ τοῖς ἄρτοις, ἀλλ’ ἦν αὐτῶν ἡ καρδία πεπωρωμένη.

records.literal_gloss: And exceedingly out of measure in themselves they were amazed, \v 52 not for they understood about the loaves, but was of them the heart hardened.

en.L: And they were utterly astonished within themselves, \v 52 for they had not understood about the loaves, but their heart had been hardened.
en.B: They were beside themselves with amazement, \v 52 for they had not grasped what the loaves showed. Their hearts had been hardened.
en.R: The followers were completely amazed. \v 52 They had not understood what the miracle of the loaves meant. Their hearts were hard, and they could not understand.

decisions.choice: understood about the loaves: what the feeding showed about who Jesus is
decisions.reason: Had they understood the feeding, they would not be so astonished that he walks on the sea.

decisions.choice: heart hardened: a mind dull and closed
decisions.reason: The heart is the place of thought. The same kind of hardness was said of Jesus' opponents in 3:5; now it is said of the disciples (8:17).

decisions.choice: had been hardened: a passive that does not say who hardened them
decisions.reason: Mark states their condition and leaves the cause unnamed.

decisions.choice: they were amazed, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "and they marveled". Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: and they could not understand
decisions.reason: Readable says what a hard heart means here, as at 3:5.

source.text: Καὶ διαπεράσαντες ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν ἦλθον εἰς Γεννησαρὲτ καὶ προσωρμίσθησαν.

records.literal_gloss: And having crossed over to the land they came to Gennesaret and anchored.

en.L: And when they had crossed over, they came to land at Gennesaret and anchored.
en.B: When they had crossed the lake, they came ashore at Gennesaret and tied up the boat.
en.R: Jesus and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers crossed the lake and came to land near the town of Gennesaret. They tied the boat up there.

decisions.choice: Gennesaret: a fertile plain on the west shore, south of Capernaum
decisions.reason: The lake was also called the Lake of Gennesaret (Luke 5:1).

decisions.choice: they came to Gennesaret, not to Bethsaida (6:45)
decisions.reason: Mark does not say why they landed elsewhere. The wind may have driven them off course.

decisions.choice: anchored: drew in to shore and moored
decisions.reason: The verb means to bring a boat into harbor.

decisions.choice: Jesus and his followers
decisions.reason: Readable names who crossed.

source.text: καὶ ἐξελθόντων αὐτῶν ἐκ τοῦ πλοίου εὐθὺς ἐπιγνόντες αὐτὸν περιέδραμον ὅλην τὴν χώραν ἐκείνην καὶ ἤρξαντο ἐπὶ τοῖς κραβάττοις τοὺς κακῶς ἔχοντας περιφέρειν ὅπου ἤκουον ὅτι ἐστίν.

records.literal_gloss: And having come out they out of the boat, immediately having recognized him \v 55 they ran around all the region that and began on the mats those sick to carry around, wherever they were hearing that he is.

en.L: And when they came out of the boat, immediately [people] recognized {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} \v 55 and ran around that whole region and began to carry around on mats those who were sick, to wherever they heard that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was.
en.B: As soon as they stepped out of the boat, people knew who {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was. \v 55 They ran all through that region and began bringing those who were ill on their mats to any place where they heard {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was.
en.R: The moment they stepped out of the boat, the people there knew it was Jesus. \v 55 They ran all over that area to tell others. Then they carried sick people on mats to any place where they heard Jesus was.

decisions.choice: mats: pallets, the poor man's bed
decisions.reason: The same word as at 2:4, 2:11.

decisions.choice: wherever they heard he was: they kept following news of him
decisions.reason: The imperfect shows people following reports of where Jesus was from day to day.

decisions.choice: recognized him: the people of that region
decisions.reason: The participle has no stated subject. The verbs that follow show it is the people there.

decisions.choice: to tell others
decisions.reason: Readable says why they ran about, which the carrying of the sick implies.

source.text: καὶ ὅπου ἂν εἰσεπορεύετο εἰς κώμας ἢ εἰς πόλεις ἢ εἰς ἀγροὺς ἐν ταῖς ἀγοραῖς ἐτίθεσαν τοὺς ἀσθενοῦντας, καὶ παρεκάλουν αὐτὸν ἵνα κἂν τοῦ κρασπέδου τοῦ ἱματίου αὐτοῦ ἅψωνται· καὶ ὅσοι ἂν ἥψαντο αὐτοῦ ἐσῴζοντο.

records.literal_gloss: And wherever he was entering into villages or into towns or into countryside, in the marketplaces they were laying the sick, and were begging him that if only the fringe of the cloak of him they might touch; and as many as touched him were being saved.

en.L: And wherever {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went, into villages or into towns or into the countryside, they laid the sick in the marketplaces and begged {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} that they might touch even the fringe of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} cloak; and as many as touched {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} were made well.
en.B: Wherever {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went, whether villages or towns or farms, people set their sick down in the marketplaces and pleaded with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to let them touch just the fringe of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} cloak. Everyone who touched {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} was made well.
en.R: Jesus went into villages, towns, and farm areas. Wherever {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went, people brought their sick friends to the marketplaces. They begged Jesus to let the sick people touch just the fringe of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} cloak. And everyone who touched {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} was healed.

decisions.choice: the fringe of his cloak: the edge, perhaps the tassels the law required
decisions.reason: The law told Israelites to wear tassels on the corners of their cloaks (Numbers 15:38-39; Deuteronomy 22:12). The word can mean those tassels or simply the edge.

decisions.choice: were made well: the verb also means were saved
decisions.reason: The same verb is used of the woman healed in 5:28 and 5:34. Healing is a sign of God's saving work.

decisions.choice: they were laying, begging, being healed: it happened again and again
decisions.reason: The tenses describe what happened in place after place.

decisions.choice: marketplaces: open squares in towns and villages
decisions.reason: The open square was where people gathered.

decisions.choice: their sick friends; the sick people
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear who was carried and who touched.
